rawIssues.issue: apiVersion '2023-05-03' predates the 2025-02-19 default perspective change. On older versions the default perspective is 'raw', so with a read token the client can return draft documents and duplicate drafts.* IDs mixed with published content. Set `perspective: 'published'` explicitly, or move to apiVersion 2025-02-19 or later and re-test queries.

No explicit `perspective` is set, so the behavior silently depends on the apiVersion default (raw before 2025-02-19, published after). Set it explicitly: 'published' for production, and 'drafts' or 'previewDrafts' only for a separate preview/draft-mode client.

`useCdn: false` bypasses the API CDN for every request. This is fine for draft or preview fetching, but for published content in production it adds latency and API load. Use `useCdn: true` for published reads, for example `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'`, and keep a separate uncached token client for previews. Note that tokens are not applied on the CDN.

projectId and dataset come straight from process.env and are typed `string | undefined`. A missing value produces a confusing runtime error or a TypeScript error. Validate them with an assertion helper (e.g. `assertValue`) that throws a clear message.

The read token is attached to a shared exported client. If this module is imported into a client component, the non-NEXT_PUBLIC token will be undefined in the browser, and bundling it risks leaking it. Keep the token client in server-only code (e.g. `import 'server-only'`) and use a token-less client for public data.
No `stega` configuration (e.g. `stega: {studioUrl}`) is set, so Visual Editing and Presentation click-to-edit overlays will not work. Enable it only for preview or draft-mode requests.

`apiVersion` is missing. Recent versions of @sanity/client warn and fall back to the legacy default API version v1 (the 'v1' default is deprecated). Set an explicit, pinned date such as '2025-02-19' so query behavior stays stable.

No `perspective` is set. The default perspective changed from `raw` to `published` at API version 2025-02-19. Without an explicit apiVersion and perspective, queries may return drafts and versions alongside published documents on older versions, but only published documents on newer ones. Set `perspective` explicitly, e.g. 'published', or use 'drafts'/'previewDrafts' only with a token for previews.

`token` is read from `process.env.SANITY_TOKEN` with no check that it is defined. A missing variable silently produces an unauthenticated client, which then fails on private datasets or writes. Validate the variable and fail fast. The token must also stay server-side, so this module should not be bundled into browser code.

The file is TypeScript (`ts`) but uses CommonJS `require`/`module.exports`. This loses type information, so `sanityClient` is untyped and `createClient` is not checked. Use `import { createClient } from '@sanity/client'` and `export const client = createClient({...})`, or `export default`.

`useCdn: false` is correct for an authenticated client that needs fresh data or writes. If this client is also used for public published reads, a second client with `useCdn: true` and no token would give better latency and caching. Note that the CDN is not used when a token is provided and the perspective is not `published`.

The 'previewDrafts' perspective was renamed 'drafts' in API version 2025-02-19. 'previewDrafts' is deprecated and the pinned 2022-11-15 version is stale. Update apiVersion and use perspective: 'drafts'.

useCdn: true is used together with a token and a drafts perspective. Draft content is private and changes frequently, so it should not be served from the cached CDN. The result can be stale or inconsistent preview data. Set useCdn: false for the preview client.

The token comes from process.env.SANITY_PREVIEW_TOKEN and may be undefined. Without a token, draft content is not returned and the failure is silent. If this client is bundled for the browser, the token would also be exposed. Keep it server-only, validate it at startup, and avoid a NEXT_PUBLIC_-style variable.

The config relies on a perspective, but the default perspective changed from 'raw' to 'published' in API version 2025-02-19. Keep the explicit perspective, and check any other clients that rely on the default when you bump apiVersion.

The query never references the `$id` parameter that is passed in. `getDraft(id)` returns the first draft post of any ID instead of the requested one. It should filter on `_id == "drafts." + $id`, or on `_id == $id` with a full draft ID.

The query depends on the raw perspective to see `drafts.*` documents, but no `perspective` is set. At apiVersion 2021-10-21 the default is `raw`, so it works today. From API version 2025-02-19 the default perspective is `published`, and a `drafts.**` query would silently return nothing after an upgrade. Set `perspective: 'drafts'` (formerly `previewDrafts`) or `'raw'` explicitly.

`useCdn` is not set explicitly, and the client is authenticated with a token to read drafts. The CDN serves only cached published content and never drafts. Set `useCdn: false` for authenticated or draft reads, otherwise results may be stale or missing and the client may warn.
`[0]` is used without an `order()`, so which draft is returned is non-deterministic. The query also has no projection, so it fetches the whole document.

The token is read from `process.env.SANITY_TOKEN` in a module that may be bundled for the browser. A token with read access to drafts must stay server-side only and never be exposed to client bundles. It should be a read-scoped token, and the code should fail clearly if the variable is missing.
The apiVersion is pinned to an old date, 2021-10-21, so the client misses newer API behavior and defaults. Use a deliberate, current date and review the changes when bumping it.
The `id` parameter in `getDraft` has an implicit `any` type. Under TypeScript strict mode this fails to compile, so annotate it as `string`.

The projection uses an empty-string key (`"": author->{name, image}`), which is invalid GROQ and will cause a query error or an unusable result. Use `"author": author->{name, image}`, or `author->{...}` if you want to spread it.

`image` in the dereferenced author returns only the raw image object with an asset reference, not a URL. Either project `image{..., asset->}` or use `@sanity/image-url` to build URLs, or the frontend won't get a usable image.
The `slug` parameter of `getPost` has no type, so it is implicitly `any` in strict TypeScript. Annotate it as `string`, and consider typing the fetch result with generics or TypeGen.

`useCdn: true` serves cached content from the API CDN, so edits may appear stale. That is fine for public production reads, but use `useCdn: false` for previews, draft content, or server-side fetches that need fresh data.

The pinned `apiVersion` '2024-06-01' predates 2025-02-19, when the default perspective changed from `raw` to `published`. Setting `perspective: 'published'` explicitly keeps behavior consistent, but consider updating the apiVersion deliberately and reviewing other changes.

`[0]` returns `null` when no post matches the slug, and the code does not handle this. Callers must handle null, for example with a 404 path. Consider a `defined(slug.current)` guard and an explicit return type.

apiVersion '2023-08-01' is older than 2025-02-19, so queries default to the 'raw' perspective. Results can include both draft and published versions of the same document, which causes duplicates in a RelatedPosts list. Pin a current apiVersion (2025-02-19 or later, which defaults to the 'published' perspective), or set `perspective` explicitly.

The `client` is created but never used, and the component returns null. There is no fetch for related posts, so the component does nothing yet. Fetching would need a useEffect or a data hook, with loading and error handling.
The apiVersion is hard-coded and stale. Define it once as a shared constant and update it on purpose after checking the changelog, so behavior stays consistent across components and doesn't drift.

The GROQ function sanity::versionOf() is only available from API version 2025-02-19. With apiVersion '2024-03-01' the query will fail or not behave as intended. Bump apiVersion to 2025-02-19 or later.

On apiVersion '2024-03-01' the default perspective is 'raw', so drafts and versions are mixed into results. From 2025-02-19 the default becomes 'published'. Set the perspective explicitly (e.g. perspective: 'published' or 'drafts') to get predictable results across API versions.
client.fetch and client.listen are called directly in the component render body. Side effects belong in useEffect, otherwise a new fetch and a new listener are created on every render.
The listen() subscription is never unsubscribed, which leaks a listener on every render and after unmount. Store the subscription and call unsubscribe() in the useEffect cleanup.
The fetch() promise result is ignored and has no error handling. The count is never used or stored in state, so Badge renders nothing useful. It also risks an unhandled rejection.

The listen filter '*[_id == $id]' only matches the exact ID. It misses the drafts.-prefixed draft and the versions.<release>. documents, so it is inconsistent with the versionOf query. Use sanity::versionOf($id) or match both IDs, and consider includeAllVersions on listen.

The listen handler is empty and does nothing with events. The listener does no work, so it should either update state or be removed. The `id` prop is also untyped, which is an implicit any in TypeScript.

The client is explicitly set to perspective 'raw'. From API version 2025-02-19 the default perspective is 'published'; 'raw' was the earlier default. Raw returns draft, published and version documents mixed together, which is rarely right for a release tool. Use 'drafts', 'published', or a release perspective stack instead.
client.listen() returns a lazy observable, so nothing runs until it is subscribed to. The result is discarded, so the listener never starts and can never be unsubscribed.

listen is called directly in the render body, which is a side effect. Every re-render would open a new listener, and there is no cleanup. Move it into useEffect, subscribe, and return a function that unsubscribes.
useClient(...).withConfig(...) runs on every render and creates a new client instance each time. Memoize it with useMemo, or pass the perspective in the config.

includeAllVersions on listen is an experimental option for release and version documents. Depending on the @sanity/client version, it may be unsupported or require a newer or vX API version. It also means events for drafts. and versions. documents will arrive, so the code must handle document ID prefixes. The perspective set on the client is not applied to listen.

client.listen() returns an Observable and nothing happens until it is subscribed to. The hook never subscribes or unsubscribes. Despite its name, it is not a React hook and has no useEffect cleanup, so listeners can leak and connections stay open if callers do not unsubscribe.

`includeResult: true` is explicit and probably unnecessary. Sanity's listener moved to the mendoza effect format and result-less events by default in newer API versions. It is also more expensive, because every event carries the full document, so use `includeResult: false` with `visibility`/`effectFormat: 'mendoza'` unless the full result is needed. Behavior depends on the client's configured apiVersion, and none is pinned here.
The client and id parameters are untyped, so this is implicitly any in TypeScript. They should be typed as SanityClient and string, and the return type should be Observable<MutationEvent>.

The listener can drop events during a disconnect. The code has no handling for reconnects, errors, or the 'welcome'/'reconnect'/'disconnect' events, and nothing refetches state after a gap. The listen call also sets no `visibility` option ('sync' vs 'query'), which affects whether events arrive before or after the document is queryable.

The listen query is a plain filter (`*[_id == $id]`), which is fine, but it must not use projections, ordering, or slices. The code carries no guard or comment about this restriction. It also sets no `tag`, which makes the listener hard to trace in request logs.
Drafts are not handled. `_id == $id` matches only the exact ID, so listening on a published ID will not see changes to `drafts.<id>` and vice versa. Use `_id in [$id, 'drafts.' + $id]` to cover both.
apiVersion '2026-09-01' looks like a future or unverified date. Pin it to a known, past, tested date so query behavior is predictable and doesn't silently change when the date becomes current.

perspective: 'published' is redundant at this apiVersion. From API version 2025-02-19 the default perspective is 'published'; before that it was 'raw'. It's harmless, but it is only needed if you might lower the apiVersion below that date, and then it matters because it prevents drafts from being returned.

useCdn: true serves cached data and can return stale content. It is fine for public, client-side reads, but for server-side rendering, previews, or reads that need fresh data after publishing, use useCdn: false or revalidate with tags/webhooks.
projectId and dataset are hardcoded. Move them to environment variables (e.g. SANITY_PROJECT_ID / SANITY_DATASET) so config can differ between environments.
The snippet doesn't show the import of createClient from '@sanity/client' (or 'next-sanity'), so check it is present.

`perspective: 'published'` is redundant on the main client. Since API version 2025-02-19 the default perspective is `published` (it was `raw` before). It is harmless, but it makes the config look like it still depends on the old default.

`perspective: 'drafts'` on the preview client only works at apiVersion 2025-02-19 or later, because it replaced `previewDrafts`. It is fine with 2025-10-01, but if someone pins an older apiVersion on this client the perspective will be rejected or behave differently. Keep the apiVersion at or above that date, or use `previewDrafts` on older versions.

The token comes from `process.env.SANITY_VIEWER_TOKEN` with no check that it is defined. If it is missing, the drafts client silently returns no draft content or fails with auth errors. The client must also only be used server-side, or the token will be bundled into browser code. Validate the env var and keep the preview client out of client bundles.
The preview client has no `stega` or `resultSourceMap` configuration (for example `stega: {studioUrl}`). Visual Editing and click-to-edit overlays will not work without it.
The projectId and dataset are hardcoded. Reading them from environment variables avoids mismatches between environments and makes it easier to switch datasets for staging and preview.

Array (stacked) perspectives containing release IDs are only supported from API version 2025-02-19. The configured 2025-03-01 satisfies this, but lowering or pinning apiVersion to an earlier date would break the perspective stack.

'drafts' is placed last in the stack, which is correct, since 'published' is implicitly appended. Don't reorder it ahead of release IDs. Release IDs such as 'rSummer' must be the release name, not the full _.releases._.rSummer document ID.

The token is read from process.env.SANITY_VIEWER_TOKEN with no validation. If it is undefined (missing env var, or client-side bundle where non-public env vars are stripped), release and draft content is silently not returned or the request fails with an auth error. Add a check that throws when the token is missing.

The client holds a read token and is exported from a module that may be imported into browser code. This risks leaking the token, so keep the module server-only (e.g. 'server-only' import) and don't expose the token via a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable.

useCdn: false is correct for a perspective that includes drafts and releases, because the API CDN doesn't serve draft or release content. Using this client for published-only public traffic would give up CDN caching, so use a separate CDN client with the 'published' perspective for that.

The apiVersion is hard-coded to a fixed date. Share it as a constant across clients and Studio config so perspective behavior stays consistent; a mismatch between clients could change how perspectives resolve.

apiVersion is computed from the current date at runtime. This defeats API version pinning, because each day (or deploy) can silently pick up new API behavior and breaking changes. Pin a fixed, explicit date string instead, such as '2025-02-19'.

With a floating 'today' date, the default perspective is 'published' rather than 'raw' because the date is at or after 2025-02-19. Queries stop returning drafts and unpublished versions, and a floating version makes this switch invisible. Set `perspective` explicitly and pin the version.

useCdn: true is hard-coded for every environment. The APICDN can serve stale data, so it is wrong for previews, draft content, server-side rendering that needs fresh data, and mutations or authenticated requests with a token. Make it environment-dependent, for example `useCdn: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'`, and disable it for preview and draft use.

Perspectives such as 'published' and 'previewDrafts' (now 'drafts') are only supported from API version 2021-03-25 onward. No perspective is set here, so draft and published behavior depends entirely on whichever version the dynamic date resolves to.
projectId and dataset are hard-coded. Move them to environment variables so the config can be reused across environments and datasets such as staging and production.
toISOString() returns a UTC date, which can be one day ahead of the local date and of the date the API recognizes. This is another reason to avoid generating the version dynamically.

apiVersion is read from an environment variable with a fallback, so the pinned version can change between environments and silently alter query behavior. Pin a single explicit YYYY-MM-DD date in code instead (the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix is also unnecessary here).

The fallback version 2023-06-21 is before 2025-02-19, so the default perspective is 'raw'. With a read token, queries return both drafts and published documents, which can produce duplicates and leak unpublished content. Set perspective: 'published' explicitly, or use apiVersion 2025-02-19 or later, where 'published' is the default.

useCdn: false is applied unconditionally. That is correct for authenticated draft or preview reads, but it means published production reads never use the API CDN, which costs latency and API quota. Use a separate CDN client without a token for public content, or set useCdn based on environment.

A read token is attached to a shared exported client. If this module is imported into client components, the token is either undefined or at risk of being bundled into browser code. Keep the token client server-only, for example by using server-only or a separate preview client.
projectId and dataset are hardcoded instead of coming from environment variables, which makes switching between staging and production harder.
createClient is used without an import from '@sanity/client' or 'next-sanity'.

apiVersion comes from process.env.SANITY_API_VERSION, which may be undefined or malformed. The client then falls back to the legacy default version '1' and logs a warning, so query behavior can silently change between environments. Pin an explicit YYYY-MM-DD string in code.

perspective: 'raw' is set explicitly. 'raw' returns both draft and published documents, with duplicates and drafts. Since API version 2025-02-19 the default perspective is 'published', and older versions default to 'raw'. Setting 'raw' on a production dataset with a token can leak unpublished drafts. Use 'published' for production reads, and use a drafts perspective only for preview with a token.

useCdn: false for what appears to be production reads gives up the edge cache, which hurts performance and increases API request costs. Use useCdn: true for public published content, and keep it false only for authenticated or draft reads that need fresh data.

A read/write token is attached to a shared exported client. If this module is imported into browser bundles, the token can leak. Keep the token only in a server-side client, and use a separate token-less client for public reads. Prefer the minimum-permission (viewer) token.

projectId and dataset are hardcoded, while apiVersion and token come from env vars. This is inconsistent and makes it harder to switch between staging and production datasets. Read all of them from environment config, and fail fast if any is missing.

apiVersion '2023-05-03' is before 2025-02-19, so the default perspective is `raw`, not `published`. With a read token, queries can return `drafts.**` documents alongside published ones, unmerged. That can leak draft content or produce duplicate documents in production. Set `perspective: 'published'` explicitly, or bump apiVersion to 2025-02-19 or later and test.

The pinned version predates Content Releases support. `versions.**` documents are not returned, and release-ID perspective stacks, `includeAllVersions` on listen, and the `sanity::versionOf`, `sanity::partOfRelease` and `releases::all()` GROQ functions are unavailable. Plugins and tooling that target Content Releases need 2025-02-19 or later.

If you bump to 2025-02-19 or later, the GROQ empty-string-key projection bug is fixed. Before that version, a `""` key silently expanded into the parent object. Queries that relied on it need the `...` spread instead, so check them before upgrading.

`useCdn: false` means every read goes to the uncached `api.sanity.io`. That is fine for preview or `drafts` perspectives and for static builds. For production frontend reads with the `published` perspective, `useCdn: true` is recommended. It gives faster, cached responses that are not rate limited, and cache misses still count against direct API limits. Use `useCdn: true` for production and keep a separate non-CDN client for previews.

A token is set. With `@sanity/client` v3 or later, a token together with `useCdn: true` is served from the CDN, and the cache is segmented per token. The token is read-scoped and is not `NEXT_PUBLIC_`-prefixed, which is good. Keep this client server-only, because the token is undefined in the browser and must never be exposed. Use the token only where drafts or private data are needed.
`projectId` and `dataset` come straight from `process.env` with no fallback or assertion. If a variable is missing, the value is `undefined` and the client fails at runtime. Validate them at startup.
`apiVersion` is missing. The client logs a deprecation warning and falls back to the outdated `v1` API. Pin a static date string such as '2025-02-19' or later, and don't compute it at runtime.

Because `apiVersion` is missing, the config resolves to `v1`. In `v1` the default perspective is `raw`, so queries return drafts and published documents side by side without merging. Starting at `v2025-02-19` the default is `published`. If you pin a newer date, queries stop returning drafts and the behaviour changes. Set `perspective` explicitly (`'published'` for production, `'drafts'` for preview) so results don't depend on the version.

At `v2025-02-19` and later, the `raw` perspective also returns `versions.**` documents. Code that relies on `drafts.**` path-prefix checks may break. `versions.**` documents are not returned in API versions before 2025-02-19.

`useCdn: false` combined with a token means every read bypasses the CDN and goes to the uncached API. That is only appropriate for server-side, build-time or preview use. For production reads that serve end users, use `useCdn: true` with the `published` perspective. The `drafts` perspective and release stacks need `useCdn: false`. Direct API calls are subject to rate and concurrency limits, while cached CDN responses are not.

The code mixes `require` and `module.exports` with a `.ts` file and the `sanityClient.createClient` namespace style. The docs show `const {createClient} = require('@sanity/client')`, or an ES `import`. This is a style and compatibility point, not an API behaviour change.

A token is passed from `process.env.SANITY_TOKEN` and no `perspective` is set. If this client can run in the browser or be shared with frontend code, the token is exposed. As of `@sanity/client` v3.0.0, a token combined with `useCdn: true` is fetched from the CDN, so a token no longer forces a CDN bypass. Keep the token server-side and use a read-only token if it is only for reads.

`useCdn: true` is combined with the `previewDrafts` perspective, which is the former name of `drafts`. Draft-inclusive perspectives are not cached by the CDN. The docs say to set `useCdn: false` for this perspective, and the client bypasses the CDN and logs a warning otherwise. For a preview client, set `useCdn: false`. A preview token with the CDN is also a poor combination. Since @sanity/client v3, a token plus `useCdn: true` goes through the CDN.
`previewDrafts` is the old name for the `drafts` perspective. Both still work, but `drafts` is preferred, so switch to `perspective: 'drafts'`.

The pinned `apiVersion` '2022-11-15' predates v2025-02-19. At that version the default perspective changed from `raw` to `published`, and `raw` began including `versions.**` documents. At the pinned version, `versions.**` documents are not returned and release-based perspective stacks (`perspective: ['release-a', ...]`) are unavailable. Content Releases, `includeAllVersions` on listen, and the `sanity::versionOf` and `sanity::partOfRelease` GROQ functions also need 2025-02-19 or later. The explicit perspective means the default change doesn't affect this client. Bump the version if you need releases or versions in preview, and test first.

The 1000-draft limit that applied to `previewDrafts` was removed as of v2021-03-25. The pinned version 2022-11-15 is after that, so the limit does not apply here. Anyone pinning an apiVersion earlier than 2021-03-25 would still hit it.

The query filters on the `drafts.**` path prefix, which only works because apiVersion 2021-10-21 predates the default-perspective change. The default perspective was `raw` before v2025-02-19. If you bump apiVersion to 2025-02-19 or later, the default becomes `published`, and drafts are excluded, so this query returns nothing. The docs recommend setting `perspective: 'drafts'` or `'raw'` explicitly rather than matching path prefixes. At 2025-02-19 and later, `raw` also includes `versions.**` documents.

The client has no explicit `perspective`, so it silently relies on the implicit `raw` default of the old pinned version. Set `perspective: 'raw'` or `'drafts'` explicitly. Note that `drafts` is not CDN-cached and needs `useCdn: false`.

`getDraft` passes `{id}` as a query parameter, but the GROQ string never references `$id`. The query returns the first draft post, not the draft with the requested id. It should filter on something like `_id == 'drafts.' + $id`, or use `sanity::versionOf($id)` at 2025-02-19 or later. `[0]` with no `order()` also makes the result arbitrary.

The pinned apiVersion 2021-10-21 is old. It does not support Content Releases features such as `sanity::versionOf` and release perspectives, which need 2025-02-19 or later and are rejected with a 400 error on earlier versions. `versions.**` documents are also not returned before that version. Bump the version deliberately: read the changelog, test in staging, and keep it as a static string.

`useCdn` is not set, and a `token` is supplied. Reading drafts needs an authenticated, non-CDN request. Since @sanity/client v3.0.0, a token combined with `useCdn: true` is served from the CDN, and draft content is not cached there. Set `useCdn: false` explicitly for draft reads, and keep the token server-side.

The projection uses an empty-string key, `"": author->{name, image}`. At apiVersion 2024-06-01 this expands the dereferenced author's fields (name, image) into the parent object, so the result is `{title, name, image}`. From 2025-02-19 the empty key no longer expands, so bumping apiVersion will silently change the result shape. Replace it with an explicit spread (`...author->{name, image}`) or a named key such as `"author": author->{name, image}`, so the behavior doesn't depend on the version.

apiVersion is pinned to 2024-06-01, which is before the Content Releases and perspective-defaults release. Release perspective stacks, `releases::all()`, `sanity::partOfRelease`, `sanity::versionOf` and `includeAllVersions` aren't available at this version. Release-based perspectives are rejected with a 400 error. Before bumping, review the other breaking changes from 2025-02-19: the default perspective changes from raw to published, and raw starts including `versions.**` documents. Setting `perspective: 'published'` explicitly is good, because it keeps the config independent of that default change.

`useCdn: true` with `perspective: 'published'` is a valid production setup. However, the same client must not be reused for preview or draft content. The `drafts` perspective and release stacks need `useCdn: false`, because they are not served from the CDN, and a token with the CDN enabled will be served from the CDN in @sanity/client v3 and later. Derive a separate preview client with `client.withConfig({useCdn: false, perspective: 'drafts', token})`.
The `slug` parameter of `getPost` has no type, so it is implicitly `any` in TypeScript. This isn't a Sanity API behavior, and the docs I retrieved don't cover it.

apiVersion '2023-08-01' is older than 2025-02-19, so the client resolves to the latest API version released on or before that date. It therefore gets the pre-Content-Releases behavior. Here the default perspective is `raw`, which returns drafts and published documents side by side, unmerged. From 2025-02-19 the default is `published`. If this component is meant to show only published related posts, queries can return draft duplicates. Bump the version and test, or set `perspective` explicitly.

Document versions (`versions.**`) are not returned for API versions before 2025-02-19. Release-based perspectives (a list of release IDs), the `includeAllVersions` parameter on listen and doc, `sanity::versionOf`, `sanity::partOfRelease` and `releases::all()` also need 2025-02-19 or later. If this component or plugin works with Content Releases, it must use `apiVersion: '2025-02-19'` or later. Bump in small steps and check the changelog.

The pinned version also predates the 2025-02-19 fix for the GROQ empty-key projection bug. Before it, an empty string key (`""`) in a projection silently expanded into the parent object. Any related-posts query that relies on this will change when the version is bumped. Replace it with the spread operator (`...`).

The client does not set a `perspective`. On this old version the implicit default is `raw`, so draft and published copies are not merged. Set the perspective explicitly (`published` for production, `drafts` for preview) so behavior doesn't change when the version is bumped. Note that `drafts` and release stacks are not CDN-cached, so use `useCdn: false` with them.
The component creates a client but never uses it (it returns `null`), so there is no query for related posts yet. This is a code-completeness issue, not an API-version one.

`sanity::versionOf()` requires apiVersion `2025-02-19` or later. The client is pinned to `2024-03-01`, so the function is unavailable. The docs say a function that doesn't exist in the pinned version returns an error. Bump apiVersion to `2025-02-19` or later, or stop using the function.

Even with `versionOf` working, `versions.**` documents are not returned in API versions before `2025-02-19`. At `2024-03-01`, `count(*[sanity::versionOf($id)])` can't count release versions. The `listen` subscription is never unsubscribed, and the `fetch` result is discarded. Both calls run in the component render body on every render, so each render opens a new listener that leaks. Move them into `useEffect`, store the fetch result in state, and unsubscribe in the cleanup function. The `useClient` hook (apiVersion `2024-03-01`) is not itself the cause. This is general React and client hygiene, not something I found in the docs.

The apiVersion '2025-02-19' is the minimum version that supports `includeAllVersions` on `/listen`, so the pin is correct. If someone lowers it, the option has no effect and no `versions.**` documents are returned. The option also needs an authenticated request, so the client must have a token or Studio auth. `perspective: 'raw'` is set explicitly. From 2025-02-19 the default perspective is `published`, so this is the right way to keep the old default. Any code that identifies drafts by a `drafts.` path-prefix check can misbehave. Use a perspective such as `drafts` or a release stack, or normalise IDs (for example with @sanity/id-utils or `getPublishedId`). Below 2025-02-19, `raw` is the default and does not include versions.

No functional problem found in the preview client's `useCdn: false` with `perspective: 'drafts'`. No definite misconfiguration found. apiVersion '2025-03-01' is on or after 2025-02-19, so the release-stack perspective is accepted. Before 2025-02-19 the API only accepts raw, published and drafts, and returns HTTP 400 'Complex perspectives are not supported for this version'. useCdn: false is correct, because release and drafts perspectives bypass the CDN.

Ordering in the perspective stack: 'drafts' is placed after the release ('rSummer'). Layers are prioritized left to right, so release versions override drafts. The docs example puts 'drafts' first, which makes drafts win. 'published' is appended automatically, but 'drafts' is not, and you have added it explicitly. Confirm that release content should take priority over drafts.
Content Releases are Enterprise-only, and the docs require @sanity/client 7.8.0 or later for release APIs. Confirm the project is on an Enterprise plan and the client is at least 7.8.0.

The token must be able to read unpublished content (drafts and release versions) for these queries. The docs don't say whether a 'viewer' token can do this, so check its permissions. Without that access, drafts and release versions may not appear. Also keep the token server-side only, because it is read from process.env.

apiVersion is computed at runtime with new Date(). The pinned version changes every day, so a new API release can change your app's behavior without a deploy. Use a hardcoded static date string instead, for example '2025-02-19' or a later date you have tested.

Because the version resolves to today's date, the client always gets the latest API behavior. That includes the v2025-02-19 breaking changes. The default perspective changes from `raw` to `published`. The `raw` perspective now also returns `versions.**` documents. The GROQ empty-string key projection (`""`) no longer expands into the parent object. Code that relied on the old defaults, such as seeing drafts without setting a perspective, will silently change. Pin a version deliberately and set `perspective` explicitly.

`useCdn: true` with no explicit perspective only suits published content. The `drafts` perspective and release perspective stacks are not CDN-cached, so previews need `useCdn: false`. The client bypasses the CDN and logs a warning if you combine them. If this client is also used for preview or draft content, create a separate client with `useCdn: false` and `perspective: 'drafts'`. For production reads, set `perspective: 'published'` explicitly.

No token is set, so this client only reads public data. If a token is added later, note that since @sanity/client v3.0.0 a token combined with `useCdn: true` is served from the CDN. In earlier client versions, a token bypassed the CDN. This is a client-version change, not an API-version change. Do not use `useCdn: true` where guaranteed-fresh data is needed, such as static builds or server-side reads right after a mutation.

apiVersion is read from NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_API_VERSION, with a fallback. The docs say to set it once as a hardcoded static date string. Here the pinned version can differ between environments and change without a code change or review. The NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix also exposes the value to the browser bundle.

The fallback '2023-06-21' is before 2025-02-19, so the default perspective is `raw`. Queries return drafts and published documents side by side, unmerged, so you can get duplicate or draft content. Under the `raw` default this applies even in production. If you bump to 2025-02-19 or later, the default becomes `published`, and `raw` also starts to include `versions.**` documents. Set `perspective` explicitly (`published` for production, `drafts` or a release stack for preview) so behavior doesn't depend on the version.

Because the version is pinned below 2025-02-19, newer features aren't available. These are release-based perspectives, `sanity::versionOf`, `sanity::partOfRelease`, `releases::all()`, and `includeAllVersions` on listen and doc. `versions.**` documents are not returned. The GROQ empty-string-key projection bug also remains, where `""` expands into the parent object. Bumping to 2025-02-19 or later changes that behavior, so replace it with `...` spread and test.

useCdn is false with a read token, so every query goes straight to the API. For published-perspective production reads, `useCdn: true` is safe and gives lower latency. Since @sanity/client v3.0.0, a token plus `useCdn: true` is served from the CDN. Keep `useCdn: false` only for preview environments that use the `drafts` perspective or release stacks, which aren't CDN-cached. The flag should depend on the environment.

`apiVersion` is read from `process.env.SANITY_API_VERSION` instead of being a hardcoded literal. If the variable is unset, `apiVersion` is `undefined` and the client throws. If it holds a moving value such as today's date, the pinned API behavior can change without a deploy. Use a static UTC date string.

`perspective: 'raw'` returns drafts and published documents side by side, unmerged. From v2025-02-19 it also returns `versions.**` (Content Release) documents, which older versions do not return. Bumping the version therefore changes the results: duplicate or extra documents appear, and code that checks `drafts.**` path prefixes may misbehave. `raw` is also not the default from v2025-02-19, where `published` is. If this client serves production content, use `published`, or `drafts` for previews. Keep `raw` only if you deliberately need every document variant.

Because `apiVersion` is unpinned, the default perspective and the `raw` contents can change when the env var is bumped. The default switched from `raw` to `published` at v2025-02-19. `raw` is set explicitly here, so the default itself won't change, but the `versions.**` inclusion will. Pin the version and test the upgrade deliberately.

`token` is combined with `useCdn: false`. Since @sanity/client v3 a token with `useCdn: true` is served from the CDN, so `useCdn: false` is the right choice for `raw` or `drafts` perspectives. It does mean every read hits the uncached API, so use `useCdn: true` with the `published` perspective for production reads. Also make sure the token stays server-side and is not exposed to browser bundles.
